text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Solidarity Election Action (AWS) has proposed the radical right-wing Liga Republikanska youth organisation's leader Mariusz Kaminski run for parliament on the AWS list. The rightist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) is also wooing Kaminski.

- AWS leader Marian Krzaklewski wants to merge all the political groupings arties which have joined the AWS electoral block in one party. The ZChN Christian National Union and the PC centrist alliance in the AWS have opposed the idea.

- An EU report on central and eastern European countries' ability to meet EU accession requirements may prove unfavourable, Poland's European Integration Committee deputy minister Jaroslaw Pietras said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Consumer and Competition Protection Office (UOKK) plans to take action against Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms firm, saying TPSA has abused its monopolist position through recent price increases of connections with cellular mobile telecoms networks, UOKK saisd.

- A shortage of professional managers and problems with obtaining commercial credits are the main barriers to development of franchising services, the Polish Franchising Association's president Jolanta Kramarz said.

- Poland will receive around 60 million European Currency Units through the PHARE-96 operational programme to finance development of transport services, agricultural infrastructure, environment protection and educational programmes this year, under an agreement signed on Monday.

- The Polish Shipping Register (PRS) has been suspended from the International Association of Classification Societies (IACS) for too liberal treatment of so-called cheap flags of convenience, the Norwegian Dagens Naeringsliv daily said.

- Swedwood wood processing firm, controlled by Sweden's IKEA household durable trading chain, has constructed a kitchen furniture plant in Goleniow, north-western Poland. The plant will employ 100 workers.
- Poland's biggest insurance firm PZU SA earned net profit of 205 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1997, it said.

- The general shareholders meeting of the PBK SA bank has decided to pass 167.4 million zlotys of the 1996 net profit of 223.8 million zlotys to increase the reserve capital and 37.5 million zlotys will fuel the bank's risk fund.
- Britain's Heath insurance brokerage firm will launch a Polish subsidiary this week and the Swiss Reinsurance Company is planning to open a representative office in Warsaw, the two companies said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Over 1,600 cash dispensers will be in operation in Poland by the end of 1997. Most of the 12 banks which have launched cash teller services are planning to double the number of dispensers and the Euronet independent chain will triple the number of its machines.

- The government plans to launch a foreign investment and export promotion agency, treasury ministry state secretary Janusz Kaczurba said. Export promotion funding now totals $10 million, divided among various sectors and industries, Kaczurba said.
- The general shareholders meeting of Chmiel Polski SA in Lublin decided to build a hops processing line worth 3.5 million marks this year, Chmiel Polski President Lech Stodolkiewicz said.

- Net-Technology, a computer systems integrator in Warsaw, plans a share issue to increase the firm's capital by 400 percent by the end of 1997 and apply for share listing on the Warsaw bourse in the first or second quarter of 1998, board member Andrzej Gorski said.
- The Progress National Investment Fund (NFI) No 11 will invest 10 million zlotys to increase share capital in its most successful subsidiaries Tymbark, Fameg and Zelmot.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's flag carrier PLL LOT has extended its Flying Bus economic ticket offer to June 15 this year. The offer covers flights on 45 routes started before August 31, LOT said.
- Stomil Belchatow, Poland's leading rubber transmission belts maker, plans to form a holding company with a group of chemical and textile firms and apply for a listing on the Warsaw bourse.
ZYCIE
- Daewo Motors Poland plans to increase assembling of Tico cars to 6,000 cars a month, the company said.

- The average monthly salary in May was highest in Warsaw, where it reached 1,278 zlotys and lowest Nowy Sacz, southern Poland, where it was 766.85 zlotys, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
PARKIET - The US Morgan Stanley investment bank's analysis of Poland's economy forecast a rise of the country's credit rating from the BBB- to BBB level in up to 18 months.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
